The total is 21, so the mean is 1.50. PART B §B2 RULE: PASSES, with zero margin.

THE SINGLE CHANGE MOST LIKELY TO RAISE EACH ITEM STILL AT 1 TO 2:
- J2: stop the lens whiteout. Gate the camera glint with an authored two-streak mask on the lens, as concept A has it, so the glint can never fill the whole lens. As a second step, raise export.smooth_normals iterations from 6 to 12; the cap highlight that capped it at 6 is gone.

- J4: re-bake the Punk's stroke layer at 2k, or close the strokes and drop short ones before the cut. The tape and seams would then be continuous lines, not sawtooth dotted chains.
- J9: raise look_motion_breath_deg from 1.5 to about 3, with look_motion_shift_deg, so the idle visibly breathes at 1 m. The taunt's near-straight arms stay; the lead ruled them.
- J11: per-swatch mark strength, placed where the hit landed. This is Game-boy's call 25; it is known and I did not re-file it.
- J13: make the placeholders' matte paints take no hard highlight, as the art's matte swatches do. Today the Kicker, Thug and Bruiser keep white highlight dots beside a matte Punk.
- J14: a finer, continuous stroke layer for the hero's wraps and trouser folds (2k, or the same closing pass). The skin knob and the belly view are Game-boy's (calls 19 and 25, and feel question 3).

findings.title: The camera-fixed lens glint whites out most of the Punk's yellow lens whenever his head tips back (every stagger, the taunt, lying)
findings.detail: The lens is the only glossy swatch. Its glint is a hard cap at look_glint_cut 0.88 on dot(N, normalize(fill_dir + VIEW)). The visor's 127-vertex normals are coarse, so when the head tips back most of the lens falls inside the 28-degree cone and clips to white. At 1 m in first person the shades then read as a white blindfold, not concept A's yellow lens with two white streaks. This happens on every hook (stagger), in the taunt, and when he lies seen from above. In the face act itself (C1) the glint is a large white wedge, about a tenth of the lens. Before the fixes, the same head-up poses showed a pale cream lens with a thin white streak. Now it is a stark white block. This, with finding 4, keeps J2 at 1.
findings.evidence: Near-white px in the LOOK-RECT head box. C14 f1215 taunt: 4,945 now against 1,636 before (ab/c14_f1215_taunt_lens_before_after.png). C14 f1468 stagger: 2,551 white against 6,075 yellow, 514 before (ab/c14_f1468_stagger_lens_pair.png). C14 f1457: 1,980 against 6. C10 f1093 lying q0: 1,136 white against 3,250 yellow. C1 f49, f109, f169, f229: 1,564 to 2,324 (c1_heads_quad.png). Code: game/fx/toon_light.gdshaderinc:113-117; game/autoload/tuning_data.gd:1084 (look_glint_cut 0.88).

findings.suggested_fix: Gate the glint with an authored streak mask on the lens: two diagonal bands as in concept A, for example in a G channel of the Punk's UV2 detail mask over slot 19. Multiply the glint by it so it can only light the streak texels, never the whole lens. The fixer listed this decal as the left-for-later route. A cheaper fallback is to raise look_glint_cut toward 0.92 and accept fewer front-view glints.

skeptic.reason: Confirmed as a real defect, not a ruled item. In every head-tipped-back pose the Punk's lens is mostly a flat white block over yellow: the taunt (about 90 frames), the stagger (about 10 to 16 frames) and the lying view from above. In upright poses it is the intended small white triangle. The fixer's own call C3 warned of the lying case and parked the painted-streak decal as "left for later", but that is not an approved departure and is not in README. It does hit judged items J2 (critical) and J5 (critical, "one small hard highlight"), and concept A has a yellow lens with two thin white streaks. It does not break the measured look-bible bar of under 3% of the visible surface: about 5k white pixels is far below 3% of the Punk's silhouette. So it keeps J2 and J5 at 1 and does not drop them to 0. Severity medium is right, and the finding's numbers hold. One correction to the suggested cheap fallback: raising look_glint_cut to about 0.92 does not remove the whiteout (see evidence).
skeptic.evidence:
The worktree is clean at f4064a4, and captures/review/c14/bot.avi (16:45) is newer than the shader files (16:36), so the recording is of this code. I did not run a new Godot capture, because another Godot process (the evidence builder) was already running. I cut frames from that avi with ffmpeg.

(1) Taunt, f1172 to f1262. Of 12 sampled head crops, 5 of the 8 taunt-phase crops (f1192 to f1262) show the lens as a wide white block with the yellow only at the right edge. The 2 before the head tips and the guard-phase frames show the small triangle. f1215 is a white slab about 60% of the lens width.

(2) Stagger, f1440 to f1535. The first three samples are guard frames with a small triangle. From about f1472 the lens is a wide white block for about 2 sampled frames (roughly 10 to 16 frames) before it recedes.

(3) C1 head quad. Three of four frames carry a white wedge about 1/6 of the lens. This is the mild, one-hard-highlight case and is acceptable on its own.

(4) Concept A (assets/source/concepts/punk_a_denim_vest.jpg). Yellow lens with two thin diagonal white streaks, so the white block is off-concept.

(5) Code and math. toon_light.gdshaderinc lines 113-117 cap smoothstep(glint_cut, ..., dot(NORMAL, normalize(fill_dir + VIEW))) at look_glint_cut 0.88. I took the default fill at yaw -35 and pitch 40, from the fill_direction() mapping in toon_materials.gd. Its half vector with VIEW is (-0.244, 0.356, 0.902), which is 25.6 degrees off the view axis. The cap's cone has a half-angle of 28.4 degrees. A visor normal facing the camera gives dot 0.902, already inside the cone. Tilting the normal 0, 10, 20, 30 or 40 degrees up gives 0.902, 0.950, 0.970, 0.959 and 0.920, all white. The standing lens is tilted about 13 degrees down (the fixer measured the mean) and gives about 0.80, so only the up-curving left portion catches the light, which is the small triangle. Any pose that points the visor at the camera or tips it up (taunt, stagger, lying seen from above) puts most of the visor's normal spread inside the cone, and the cap clips all of it to white. A cap threshold cannot make a streak. It can only make a blob that grows with the angle.

(6) The cheap fallback fails. At cut 0.92 the tipped-up normals still give 0.95 to 0.97, so the taunt would still whiten. Only a cut near 0.97 or higher would shrink it, and that deletes the front-view glint (0.80 to 0.90). The fixer already measured 0.93 as a mere speck, or nothing, in C1/C2/C4. The glint's coverage has to come from a mask, not from the threshold.
skeptic.root_cause: The glint is a pure angular cap, smoothstep at glint_cut 0.88 on dot(N, normalize(fill_dir + VIEW)). The camera-fixed fill's half vector is only 25.6 degrees off the camera-facing direction, and the cap's cone is 28.4 degrees, so any lens normal that faces the camera, or tilts up to about 50 degrees, lands inside the cone and clips to white. The standing visor tilts about 13 degrees down, so it only catches the light at its up-curving corner and the glint is a small triangle. When the head tips back (taunt, stagger) or is seen from above (lying), the whole visor swings into the cone and goes white. A cap on the angle cannot produce a streak, and the lens's coarse 127-vertex normals make the edge blocky. The glint has no spatial authoring, so the lens needs an authored streak mask that gates it.

findings.title: The striking glove at contact is a featureless charcoal dome over a fifth to a quarter of the view (J3)
findings.detail: At the jab's and the cross's hit frames the Punk's glove turns its back to the lens. It fills a large part of the view as two flat charcoal tones: no knuckle ridge, no strap line, no bare finger. It reads as a blob, not a fist, which is exactly what J3 rules out for strikes. At the chin the fists read (thumb, knuckle bumps, fingertips). The glove has no ink zone, so even its back carries no line. F-punk and the slice gate logged this as a gap, and no fix wave touched it. It is what keeps the critical J3 at 1.
findings.evidence: C4 f62 (punk_jab_hit): 16.6% of the frame within 6 of (45,42,69), plus 8.3% near (56,55,68). C4 f90 (punk_cross_hit): 16.3% plus 2.6% (c4_jabcross_quad.png, c4/sheets/c4/stills/c4_f62_punk_jab_hit.png). This is the same as V1's f60-f63 and f89-f93.

findings.suggested_fix: Give the glove's back something to read: an ink zone on the glove slot with a knuckle-ridge line and the strap's edge (pipeline.json detail_bake zones), rebuilt with run.py --check. Or roll the hand bone in the art's bind so the knuckle face turns to the lens at contact (not the move clip, per A20).

skeptic.reason: Confirmed as a real, unlogged-as-approved gap against the plan's critical J3 ("gloved fists read as fists ... in strikes (strap, knuckles), not blobs"). At the jab (f62) and cross (f90) hit frames the striking glove is a featureless two-tone navy/charcoal dome covering about a fifth of the frame, with no knuckle ridge, strap or bare finger. It is not a SPEC departure, a logged default call, or one of the "known and ruled" items. The lead's override final-v1-02 (OUT) ruled only the glove's size against concept A and the A5 fist box. F-punk and the slice gate recorded the dome as an open weakness, not an approved departure, and V1 filed it as a score note, so no fix wave touched it. Severity "medium" is fair: J3 at 1 still meets the pass rule's critical floor, and fixing it would lift J3 to 2. One correction to the reviewer's suggested fix: the bind-roll route is the weaker one (see root_cause). A config-only "ink zone" (a threshold change on the existing top-hat) will not work either, because the source texture has no lines to extract.
skeptic.evidence:
Looked at the reviewer's recordings at f4064a4 (captures/review/c4/sheets/c4/stills/c4_f62_punk_jab_hit.png, c4_f90_punk_cross_hit.png, c4_f63 hit_next, crops/c4_f40_hands.png). I did not re-record: the reviewer's recording is at the same commit, and a second recording would have taken a capture slot beside the evidence builder's.

1. Pixel counts, from a PNG decoder I wrote, on the 1600x900 stills: f62 has 16.6% of pixels within 6 of (45,42,69) plus 8.3% near (56,55,68); f90 has 16.3% plus 2.6%. These match the finding's figures exactly. The glove is one flat dome with the flash starburst on it. In the f40 guard crop the same glove reads as a fist (thumb, knuckle bumps, bare fingertips), so the defect is specific to the strike's close range.

2. Mask content, from a pure-Python parse of assets/export/characters/punk/punk.glb and punk_detail.png. The Body mesh's 13,995 vertices are one mesh. Each hand has about 750 glove triangles (palette slot 2) and about 285 bare-skin finger triangles (slot 6). Sampling the UV2 ink mask (R > 127) over the glove triangles gives 17 of 3,016 samples on the left glove (0.6%) and 4 of 3,004 on the right (0.1%). The fingers' skin gives 0.2-1.0%. The whole mask has only 3,791 ink texels of 1,048,576. So the glove has effectively no ink.

3. assets/source/characters/punk/pipeline.json palette.detail_bake.zones lists only face_skin, nose, strap (a head-height box), cap, boots, laces and shades_frame. There is no glove zone, and `no_ink_slots` is [19] only.

4. Why a zone cannot make lines. The mask is "the thin dark lines of the source texture and nothing else" (tools/pipeline/pipe_detail.py docstring). I extracted the Tripo fist's baked texture (e70776cb_gen.glb) and it is flat grey with no printed stitching, plate edge or strap line. The concept's glove (parts/fist/views/fist_left.jpg) has a stitched dorsal plate outline, a strap and scalloped knuckles. Tripo kept the plate only as a faint relief (e70776cb_preview.webp).

5. Skinned probe (a scratch GUT test, deleted afterwards, git status clean). Pose: punk.glb on a rig 1 m from the lens at pitch -6, played to the jab's and the cross's startup frames. Of the lens-facing glove area (solid-angle weighted), the dorsal face (rest-local +z) is 49% at jab contact and 46% at cross contact. The finger end (-y) is 35% and 38%, and the sides are 13-16%. The guard has the same dorsal share, 57-59%. The nearest glove triangle is 0.18 m from the lens at contact. The dorsal face is what the lens sees both in the guard and in the strike, so rolling the hand would also change the guard, where the glove reads.
skeptic.root_cause:
Three things combine; the first two are in the pipeline.

(a) Nothing draws a line on the glove, and the mask cannot, as built. The Punk's ink bake (tools/pipeline/pipe_detail.py, driven by blender_palette.py) is only a black top-hat of the dense source texture. The Tripo glove texture is flat grey with no lines, so the glove gets about 0.1-0.6% ink. The hero's pipeline has two terms the Punk's lacks. One is an analytic swatch-border term (plate edge, strap) and the other is a geometry crease term. See tools/pipeline/player_detail.py.

(b) The glove's detail is stripped at the swatch level. F-punk-fix F1 threw the generated cuff and strap away for a collar. The glove, plate and cuff are all one flat dark swatch (slot 2, "dark_grey", shared with the tank top), because the palette has no slot to spare (7 is the contract's maximum). The concept's stitched plate and strap therefore survive only as faint relief. The relief is then flattened by the export's smoothed normals (`export.smooth_normals`, assets/source/characters/punk/pipeline.json:561, applied in tools/pipeline/blender_export.py), so the toon bands carry no knuckle or plate edge.

(c) The pose and the range. At contact the glove is 0.18 m from the lens, so the dorsal and knuckle-end faces fill 16% of the view. At that size two flat tones read as a blob. The Punk's hit-frame hand orientation comes from the A20-frozen move clips, so it is not the cause. The probe shows the hand already shows its dorsal face to the lens in the guard, where it reads.

findings.title: The sharp cut on the 1k ink masks draws sawtooth strokes that break into dotted chains at 1 m (tape, vest seams, the hero's wraps and trouser folds)
findings.detail: look_detail_cut 0.15 with a one-pixel fwidth edge makes the lines hard-edged, which fixes V1's and V3's grey smears. But the shape still follows the bilinear 1k mask: 1.7 mm texels, magnified 3-9 px at 0.2-1 m. The tape's strands come out as sawtooth bars whose faint ends break into rows of dots. The vest's seams are dash-dot lines, and the hero's trouser folds are irregular black blots. The tape and wraps also read heavier than the concepts' thin pen lines. This keeps J4 (critical) at 1 and is the part of J14's 1 that is in our hands.

findings.suggested_fix: Clean the stroke layer before the bake rather than in the shader. Close each stroke by 1-2 texels and drop pieces shorter than a minimum length, so a strand is one continuous line with ends that thin out instead of breaking into dots. Or bake the stroke layer at 2k (0.85 mm texels), the optional bake both fixers skipped. Apply this in pipe_detail.py for the Punk and player_detail.py for the hero, keep the shader's cut, and rebuild with --check.

skeptic.reason: Confirmed in a narrowed form: the Punk's baked ink mask is fragmented into dots, which reproduces as dotted and sawtooth tape strands and dashed seams at 2x to 4x, and mildly at 1x. The finding's premises are partly wrong. (a) The hero's mask is not fragmented, because the wave-1 `clean` already despeckles it. (b) The reviewer's "1.7 mm texels, 3-9 px at 0.2-1 m" is wrong for the Punk: his texels are 2.6 mm, about 1.2 px at 1 m and 2.3 px at 0.5 m. (c) The 2k bake option is excluded by SPEC §10 and A18 (1k) and by the lead's note, so the fix stays at 1k and needs no spec change. (d) The despeckle option was considered and not taken in call W1 of F-punk.md, on the premise that the Punk's lines are 0 or 1 in texture space. My measurement shows that premise does not hold after the bake. The severity is cosmetic, with a payoff of J4 (critical) and J14 going from 1 to 2.
skeptic.evidence:
METHOD. No Godot or Blender process was started: P3-evidence's capture was running and RAM was nearly full. I reproduced from the reviewer's recordings in the worktree at f4064a4, whose tree is clean, using ffmpeg crops. I parsed the GLBs' UV2 in pure Python and decoded the mask PNGs with zlib.

REPRODUCED (captures/review/c2/sheets/c2/stills/c2_f109_idle_t060.png, crop x930-1170, y500-740, 4x nearest). The tape strands are sawtooth bars about 2 texels per step. The lowest strands at the wrist are chains of dots and short dashes. At 2x (crops/c2_f109_body.png) the lower strands are still visibly dashed, and at 1x there are dotted ends at the wrist. The strokes are hard-edged and bold, and heavier than the concept's thin pen tape (punk_a_denim_vest.jpg). The hero's wrap in ab/c11_wrap_before_after.png is hard and has a few broken dash ends. The trouser folds in pa1_f324 are small irregular black blots.

MEASURED, mask content (1k PNG, 8-connected pieces at the shader's cut 0.15 = 38/255):
- punk_detail.png: 1,144 pieces. 886 are 6 texels or smaller, which is 78% of pieces and 1,854 of 7,366 ink texels (25%). The median piece is 2 texels, only 70 pieces exceed 20 texels, and 59% of the non-zero texels are partial values of 8-100.
- player_detail.png: 917 pieces. Only 106 are 6 texels or smaller (266 texels, 0.6% of ink), 599 exceed 20 texels, and 10% of non-zero texels are partial.

MEASURED, texel density (GLB TEXCOORD_1, mm of surface per mask texel):
- Punk: 2.6 mm everywhere. UV2 covers only 424,251 of 1,048,576 texels (40%). The fixer's and the reviewer's "1.7 mm" assumes the whole atlas is used.
- Hero: forearms 1.7 mm mean (median 1.55), legs 2.0 mm.
At 90 degree FOV and 900 px, a texel on screen is about 1.2 px at 1 m and 2.3 px at 0.5 m for the Punk. For the hero it is about 2.3 px at 0.4 m and about 5 px at 0.2 m. So 3-9 px at 1 m is wrong. It only fits the hero at less than 0.4 m, and the hero's dots are already cleaned.

CHECKED AGAINST SPEC AND PLAN:
- SPEC §10 and the plan say "1k detail mask", and README's A18 departure is 1024 px. `fix-final-toon-light-and-ink.md` C2 says "The optional 2k mask: not taken (the lead's note)". F-punk.md W1 says a 2048 mask was "not taken, A18 and test_art_contract say 1k".
- The hero's "close and drop short pieces" is already in `player_detail.py`: `detail.clean` opens strokes by 2 texels and removes pieces under 6 texels (fix-final-toon-light-and-ink.md C3).
- F-punk.md W1 rejected "the hero's harden and open-and-despeckle passes on the Punk's mask" because "the Punk's smoothstep is already in texture space (lines are 0 or 1)". That premise holds in texture space but not after the bake.
- `fix-final-punk-detail-zones-and-strap.md` §4 already logged the tape as "bold and a little ragged at 4x ... thicker than the concept's pen line ... wave 1's cut (0.15) and the 1k mask". The lead's wave-2 ruling for final-v1-01 was "finishes the threshold if the Punk still shows soft or dotted lines". It is not in the KNOWN AND RULED list.

ROOT CAUSE: see root_cause.
skeptic.root_cause: The Punk's mask comes from `pipe_detail.bake()`, which takes one bilinear tap per 2.6 mm UV2 texel from a 2048 source's black top-hat, `bilinear(shape(ink, lo, hi), uv)`. The source lines are about 1 to 3 mm wide, so they are undersampled about 2x with no area filter, and the bake has no closing or minimum-piece step. A strand therefore comes out 1 to 2 texels wide with dropouts, and its faint ends become isolated 1 to 6 texel pieces. That is 886 of the 1,144 pieces above the cut, 25% of the ink texels, with a median piece of 2 texels. The shader then draws what it is given. `toon.gdshader` cuts the bilinear mask at 0.15 with a one-pixel edge, so each texel-scale gap or diagonal step shows as a dot or a sawtooth step. The cut also widens the 1-texel lines to about 2.7 texels, which is the weight. The lead tuned the cut to 0.15 because 0.35 to 0.5 fragments the strands. The hero is different: `player_detail.py` already opens and despeckles its strokes, so its pieces are long and its residual roughness is the weight and ragged edge of 2-3 texel strokes magnified 2-5 px at 0.2-0.4 m, a hand-inked look the fixer accepted. A secondary cause is that the Punk's UV2 fills only 40% of the 1k atlas (`smart_project` with an island margin of 0.004, then `pack_islands`, in `blender_palette.py` around lines 549-550). That is why the Punk's texel is 2.6 mm and not 1.7 mm.

skeptic.root_cause: Shading normals are smoothed by pipe_normals.smooth_normals() in tools/pipeline/pipe_normals.py. It is a crease-preserving neighbour blend, called by blender_export.smooth_shading_normals() with the rounds taken from export.smooth_normals.iterations in assets/source/characters/punk/pipeline.json (line 562, value 6, crease_deg 50, falloff 2.0). The toon shader (game/fx/toon_light.gdshaderinc, light()) cuts its bands on the interpolated NORMAL, taking the stronger of dot(NORMAL, sun) and the fill (look_fill_strength 0.4), with the sun's shadow map dimming only the sun's term. The head is a 15k-triangle decimated mesh with few triangles over the face, and the normal varies from vertex to vertex over a few triangles. Each band contour is therefore a chain of straight segments, one per triangle, so it reads as a polygon-edged patch. 6 rounds leave enough vertex-to-vertex variation for that; 12 flatten the face's normal field so the contour becomes one long soft curve. 6 was chosen in F-punk F4 (docs/milestones/M4-calls/F-punk.md) only because 12 made the cap's and forehead's hard highlight a large white slash. That puts white dots on the Kicker's and Thug's helmets and knees and pale streaks on their forearms beside the matte Punk. It is not covered by a ruling. skeptic.evidence:
Code: game/fx/toon_materials.gd apply_look() lines 179-180 set spec_strength to 0.0 only for room surfaces (ENVIRONMENT, GRID), else look_spec_strength 0.5, for CHARACTER, ART and PROP. The glossy meta set in _make() only switches spec_gloss between look_spec_gloss (3) and 1. game/actors/rig_paint.gd:44 is the only game caller of character(). It passes glossy only for Paint.DARK, so every other primitive paint is spec_strength 0.5 at gloss 1. toon_light.gdshaderinc line 111 adds spec * spec_strength * spec_gloss * taken, and taken is swatch_spec, which is 1.0 on a flat-painted material. skeptic.root_cause: ToonMaterials.apply_look() gives the CHARACTER kind (and PROP) the full look_spec_strength regardless of the paint's glossy flag. The flag only scales spec_gloss (x3 or x1).
